summary: Norman Mosley Penzer was an Indologist who earned his M.A. at the University of Cambridge (~1910–1914). In 1925, he held memberships and fellowships in the Folklore Society, Royal Anthropological Institute, Royal Asiatic Society, Royal Geographical Society, and Geological Society.
Norvin J. Hein worked in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Franklin Edgerton. By 1965, he was Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University.

Nosei Fuji specializes in Buddhist studies and studied at Dongguk University (1986). His career includes positions at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, the Buddhist Cultural Institute, and Ryukoku University, where he served as Professor of Buddhist Studies (2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at the University of Oslo and the Norwegian Academy of Music, he held posts at the NCC Center, the University of Oslo (~1986–2011), Notam, and Oslo Metropolitan University.

Noémie Verdon is a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne (up to 2015) under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, later holding an attested post at Kyoto University (2018–2019).

Noël Peri specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology after studying at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice (~1883–1888). He taught Western music at Tokyo University of the Arts (1896–1906) and served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient starting in 1907.

Nyanaponika Thera worked in Buddhist studies, studying under Nyanatiloka Mahathera, Anton Walter Florus Gueth, and Mahasi Sayadaw, and attending the University of Peradeniya. He headed the Forest Hermitage (1952) and co-founded and directed the Buddhist Publication Society (1958–1988).

Nyingcha Duoji is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Boston University and earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp and instruction of Mark Elliott.

Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also served as a teacher to Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Nyoshul and Katok Monasteries, as well as under Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, teaching numerous students.
Nyoten Jinbo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami and held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Odette Viennot specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Philippe Stern and attended the École du Louvre and École Pratique des Hautes Études. She held appointments at the Guimet Museum (1951) and the CNRS (~1954–1975).
Odolen Smékal was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Vincenc Pořízka and earned his Ph.D. from Charles University in 1952. He taught Hindi at Charles University beginning in 1954.

Ofer Peres is an Indologist working in religious studies. He has been affiliated with the South Asia Institute at Heidelberg University and held an attested post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2026).

Ogyen Trinley Dorje is active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, the 14th Dalai Lama, Bokar Rinpoche, Pema Donyo Nyinje, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, and Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and has taught Khenpo Sherab Püntsok.
Ohryu Matsushima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at and subsequently held a post at Ryukoku University (attested 2003).

Oktiabrina Volkova worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Bidia Dandaron, later teaching at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (1952–1956) and working at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1956–1981).

Olaf Hansen was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar who completed his Ph.D. and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg under Hans Reichelt. His academic posts included the University of Jena, Free University of Berlin (1950–1968), and Kiel University.

Olav Hackstein works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, earning his Dr. phil. from the University of Freiburg (1993). He has held positions at Halle-Wittenberg, University of Pennsylvania, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and University of Munich (2008).

Oldřich Friš was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný. He held academic posts at Palacký University Olomouc (1948–1951) and Charles University (beginning 1950), succeeding Lesný in 1954.
